gospelTitle: The Lesson of the Fig Tree

retelling.text: Jesus tells His disciples a parable about the fig tree and all the other trees. When the buds open, everyone knows summer is close, and in the same way, when they see these signs, they should know that God's Kingdom is near.
He assures them, with great certainty, that this generation will not pass away before all of this has happened. Heaven and earth will not last forever, but His words will never pass away.

reflectionTitle: Friday of the Thirty-fourth Week: Watching for the Kingdom
reflection: As the Church year draws to a close, our readings turn toward the end of all things, and toward the new beginning God has promised.
In the First Reading, John sees evil bound, the dead standing before God's throne, and the book of life opened. Nothing is hidden, and nothing is forgotten.
Yet the vision does not end in judgment. It ends with a new heaven, a new earth, and a holy city coming down from God like a bride prepared for her husband.
The Psalm gives us the heart's response: our souls long for God's house, where even a sparrow finds a home. God does not stay far away. He chooses to live among His people.
In the Gospel, Jesus uses something very ordinary, a fig tree. Anyone can see new buds and know that summer is near.
He asks us to read the signs of our lives with the same calm attention. God's Kingdom is not only a distant event. It is already drawing near, quietly, in what we notice and how we respond.
What is surprising is His confidence. Heaven and earth will pass away, but His words will not. Everything we lean on for security is temporary, except His promise.
That is also a challenge. It is easy to build our days on deadlines, results and reputation, as if those things would last forever.
In the workplace, this can free us. We can work hard and lead well without being ruled by fear of failure or by the praise of others.
Watching for the Kingdom means paying attention to people: the colleague who is struggling, the employee who needs encouragement, the family member who just needs us to listen.
At home, it means choosing patience and forgiveness now, instead of waiting for a better moment that may not come.
A good leader serves as someone who will answer to a higher throne. Fair decisions, honest words and quiet kindness are small buds of the Kingdom.
We do not need to fear the end. We need to be ready, and readiness looks like faithful love in ordinary things.
So today, let us stand tall, lift our heads, and trust that our redemption is near.
message: Everything we depend on will pass away except Christ's word, so let us build our work, our homes and our leadership on faithful love today.
